products.name: Real-Time CDP Collaboration
products.title: Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration
products.what: With Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration, you can discover, activate, and measure high-value audiences without relying on third-party cookies.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration overview

products.status: current, with a question for Adam
products.status_note: Adobe's guide puts a Limited Availability badge on 46 of its 52 pages and a regional availability banner on 33 of them, yet its release notes say the product became generally available in the United States in February 2025 and list three later regional launches (Australia and New Zealand, Canada, then Europe, the Middle East and Africa), and Measurement general availability in March 2026. The badge links to the product description, which has no availability wording at all. Read together, the label is about regions, not about an early program. Whether that passes Adam's rule is his call: see the top of the trail.

status_source.quote: Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform (CDP) Collaboration is currently available in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, with global availability coming soon.

status_sources_more.quote: is now generally available in the United States.
Measurement reporting is now generally available in Collaboration.
It is automatically available to Real-Time CDP Prime and Ultimate customers in these regions.

products.notes: Collaboration is a clean room: two parties match audiences on hashed keys, see overlaps, send audiences to each other and measure campaigns, and neither sees the other's records. Every activity uses Collaboration Credits, and the two parties agree in the connection settings how the credits are split. An advertiser account can source 25 audiences and a publisher account 250, and no audience under 1,000 members can be activated. The role (advertiser or publisher) and the region of an account cannot be changed after setup, and match keys cannot be added to a connection once it is established, so CO02 starts with the match key strategy. Measurement (CO05, XD03) only shows in a project when the Measurement use case was chosen in the connection settings, and attribution reports need the advertiser's conversion data, which today can come from Experience Platform only. One use case, Expansion Models, is left out of these lines: see left_out. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: An active Real-Time CDP Collaboration license, or a Real-Time CDP Prime or Ultimate license in a region where Adobe offers Collaboration
Your client's organization in one of the regions Adobe lists: the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, or Europe, the Middle East and Africa
Collaboration Credits on the order: every sourcing, activation and measurement activity uses them
System or product administrator access to Experience Platform, to set up roles and users
A match key strategy agreed before account setup: keys cannot be added to a connection after it is established
Brand name, description, logo (SVG) and a team contact email for the account
At least one collaborator (a publisher, another brand or an advertising platform) willing to connect
No more than 25 sourced audiences for an advertiser account or 250 for a publisher account, and at least 1,000 members in any audience that is activated

products.name: Marketing Campaign Analytics
products.title: Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics (formerly Adobe Mix Modeler)
products.what: Marketing Campaign Analytics is an Adobe Experience Cloud application that measures campaigns and optimizes planning holistically across all channels: paid, earned, and owned.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics guide

products.status_note: Mix Modeler is now Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics. The Experience League guide has moved: every /en/docs/mix-modeler/ address answers with a redirect to /en/docs/marketing-campaign-analytics/. The product description on helpx.adobe.com is still titled Mix Modeler (effective 13 August 2024), and schema and dataset names inside the product still start with AMM.

status_source.quote: Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics is the evolution and rebranding of Adobe Mix Modeler

products.notes: Marketing Campaign Analytics joins marketing mix modeling, which works on summary data such as weekly spend by channel, with multi-touch attribution, which works on event data, and turns the models into budget plans. Most of the effort is data: every channel's spend, the conversions and the outside factors have to be in Experience Platform datasets with a date, a granularity and a channel before anything can be modeled, which is why MM02 and MM03 carry the most hours. Multi-touch attribution is optional and is switched on per model; the event-level scores that the Customer Journey Analytics and Real-Time CDP lines use exist only for models that have it on. Rescoring a model does not update a plan built on it: a new plan is needed, which MM06 allows for. Two features are left out of these lines (full funnel modeling, and the switch that sends scores to Customer Journey Analytics through a connection and data view Adobe creates): see left_out. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: A Marketing Campaign Analytics license, sized by the number of conversions a year your client wants to measure (the product description still calls it Mix Modeler)
An Experience Platform sandbox for it; the license includes up to 5 sandboxes and 10 active models
Spend and marketing effort data for every channel in scope, with a date, a granularity and a channel on every row
Conversion data (orders, revenue, leads) for the same period, and any internal or external factors your client wants in the model
Enough history: a model is trained on at least one year of data, and Adobe's default is the last two years
A Permissions role with the Marketing Campaign Analytics resource, a sandbox and dataset and schema permissions
For data from Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Snowflake and similar sources: the Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors add-on
No more than 30 marketing touchpoints for one conversion in a model

products.name: GenStudio for Performance Marketing
products.title: Adobe GenStudio for Performance Marketing
products.what: GenStudio for Performance Marketing is an application built on Adobe's generative AI platform. It enables marketing teams to create, manage, and optimize campaign content for paid media, email, and display ads.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe GenStudio for Performance Marketing user guide

products.status_note: Name unchanged. Several parts of the guide carry a Beta badge and are kept out of the lines: Campaigns, creating LinkedIn experiences, banner experiences, starter templates and image variants.

status_source.quote: GenStudio for Performance Marketing is an Adobe CX Enterprise product and uses that product ecosystem's extensibility framework.

products.notes: GenStudio generates ad and email variants from templates, brand guidelines and approved assets, routes them through review, sends approved ads to the ad platforms switched off for a last check there, and reports how each creative performs. Nothing can be generated until the brand guidelines are in, and nothing can be activated or measured until an ad account is connected, so GS02 and GS04 come before any campaign. Activation needs the campaign and the ad set to exist in the ad platform already: GenStudio does not create them. The first connection brings in six months of history, which can take one to five days, and channel data is kept for 13 months. The base license is 10 power users, 20 collaborators, 5 brands and 60,000 generative actions a year. GS03 covers email, Meta and display templates only; creating LinkedIn experiences is left out: see left_out. Insights runs on Experience Platform and Customer Journey Analytics components that Adobe creates and manages for GenStudio: they are not your client's own Customer Journey Analytics, and resetting the production sandbox removes them. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: A GenStudio for Performance Marketing license; the base includes 10 power users, 20 collaborator users, 5 brands, 2 terabytes of storage and 60,000 generative actions a year
An Adobe system administrator to assign licenses in the Admin Console; the default product profiles must not be changed
Brand, product and persona guidelines ready to upload or enter: editors cannot start until the brand is set up
A user group and an Admin Console project for Brands permissions, set up by the system administrator
For each ad platform: an ad account with full permission to manage campaigns and ads, connected by a system manager or editor
Campaigns and ad sets already created in the ad platform: GenStudio does not create them
One to five days for the first import of six months of history from a newly connected ad account

notes: Names. Mix Modeler is now Adobe Marketing Campaign Analytics, and every name and scope in this file uses the current name. The id stays mmm. Collaboration lifecycle, for Adam: the guide badges the product Limited Availability on 46 of 52 pages and carries a regional banner on 33, while its release notes say generally available in the United States (February 2025), then Australia and New Zealand, Canada, and Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and Measurement general availability (March 2026). The badge links to the product description, which has no availability wording. See the top of the trail.

Collaboration pages disagree on destinations: the destinations overview lists Experience Platform, Amazon S3, Snowflake, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, SFTP and Data Landing Zone as available and the July 2026 release note calls cloud storage destinations self-service, while the quick start and the use cases page still say to contact Adobe for a cloud destination. XD02 covers the Experience Platform destination only.

Collaboration measurement (XD03) is marked optional in Adobe's quick start, so it defaults off, but attribution reports in the Measure workspace cannot run without it. The quick start also says full reporting functionality may require backend enablement.
collab-mmm and collab-cja are no longer in the connections list. They are under left_out with the Oct 30 sentence, which could not be read again today.

Marketing Campaign Analytics license terms (helpx product description, effective 13 August 2024, still under the Mix Modeler name): licensed per 1,000,000 conversions, with 10 active models and up to 5 sandboxes. The Oct 30 note said Privacy and Security Shield must be licensed with Mix Modeler. The sentence reads differently: Privacy and Security Shield is an add-on, and a client that buys it must buy it for every Experience Platform application it licenses, Mix Modeler included. Check current terms before quoting.

Marketing Campaign Analytics: event-level scores, used in XD04, XD07 and XD08, exist only when multi-touch attribution is turned on for the model. Rescoring a model does not change plans already built on it.

Real-Time CDP lookalikes (XD04): Real-Time CDP Prime includes 5 and Ultimate 20 active look-alike audiences in production sandboxes. The base audience must be created in Experience Platform on the default merge policy, and look-alike features switch off automatically in low-usage environments. A client that licenses Marketing Campaign Analytics on its own has no right to Experience Platform's profile and segmentation services, so XD04 needs Real-Time CDP.

Content Analytics and Customer Journey Analytics: Content Analytics is a standalone license configured inside Experience Platform and Customer Journey Analytics, and it can no longer be bought as an add-on to Customer Journey Analytics. Its product description lists audience publishing (25 refreshing audiences) among its own limits, so XD06 no longer carries needs: cja. The cja-ca lines still assume the client licenses Customer Journey Analytics with its own journey data.

Content Analytics limits from Experience League: featurization is English only, it is not a HIPAA-ready service, Privacy and Security Shield labeling does not cover its experiences and assets, one configuration per sandbox, and the paid media channel is not available for deployments on AWS. The guided configuration warns not to use the Google Ads (beta) card when setting up the source.

Paid media sources: the Google Ads (V2) page says the source is available as part of the Customer Journey Analytics SKU. The Meta Ads page names Mix Modeler, Customer Journey Analytics, GenStudio for Performance Marketing and Content Analytics as applications the source feeds, which is the only Experience League page found that puts those names together. It says Meta data reaches Mix Modeler via Snowflake, which no Marketing Campaign Analytics page explains, and Snowflake is among the Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors that product licenses separately.

ca-gspm channel overlap: GenStudio activates to Meta, LinkedIn, Google Campaign Manager 360, Amazon Ads, Innovid, TikTok, YouTube, ChatGPT and The Trade Desk. Content Analytics paid media covers Meta and Google Ads. The measurable overlap is Meta. GenStudio places YouTube ads through Google Ads Demand Gen campaigns, so a Google Ads source may cover those too; Adobe does not say.

GenStudio's own Insights also reports on creative attributes. It runs on Experience Platform and Customer Journey Analytics components Adobe manages for GenStudio and keeps channel data for 13 months. The Oct 30 note quoted Adobe's Content Analytics FAQ on the difference between the two; that FAQ is on business.adobe.com and was not read today.
